#2731. 3 ‘things I think’ before Giants-Eagles: Critical 5-day stretch has arrived

The division-leading New York Giants begin a season-defining five-day stretch on Sunday when they face the Philadelphia Eagles. NFC East games against the Eagles and Washington Commanders book-ending that stretch, with an intriguing NFL trade deadline sandwiched in the middle.

After the Giants defeated the Houston Texans in overtime in Week 7, head coach John Harbaugh said these post-bye division contests would be "The two most important games of the season" because they "will set the direction for the rest of the season."

Giants 4-2-1Dallas Cowboys 3-5Commanders 2-4-1Eagles 2-6

Two victories in the next five days would get the Giants to 6-2-1, and build the Giants a cushion they might need with the schedule getting tougher over the season's last eight weeks.

It is a fair criticism of the Giants that they have played only one team thus far with a .500 record, and were blown out by the Los Angeles Rams in that game. Over their last eight games, the Giants face the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2), San Francisco 49ers (6-1), Seattle Seahawks (4-4), Cleveland Browns (5-3), and Detroit Lions (5-2), along with the Cowboys, Eagles, and Indianapolis Colts.

Strip away all the chatter about the Giants' losing streak in Philadelphia, Joe Milton making his first career start at quarterback for the Eagles, Cam Skattebo's availability, and everything else and the truth is this is a game the Giants should win. They are the better team, and they have much more to play for.

"It's just a really important game for our team," Harbaugh said.

"Division game, man. Division game. We're trying to win the division first. That's our first goal here. This game will go a long way toward that. That's why it's so important. Division games are big. Division games on the road are really big. Those are big wins if you can get them. They're tough to get. It's a big challenge. We're excited about the opportunity, but we understand it's a daunting challenge."

If the Commanders can defeat the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, it is possible Washington emerges as the biggest threat to the Giants in the division.

A split of the Eagles and Commanders games wouldn't be devastating, but it would make the path to the playoffs more treacherous for the Giants.

Losing both games would bring serious questions regarding whether the Giants are actually ready to capitalize on the opportunity they have.

In-between, of course, is the trade deadline. Will the Giants get Jonathan Taylor? A lesser back to supplement what they have? Help at defensive tackle? How much will they be willing to give up to get any of that?

Buckle up, Giants fans. It is going to be a fascinating five days.

If Cam Skattebo is out due to his hamstring injury, as seems likely, the Giants know they will get a solid professional effort from Devin Singletary. What they will get from Gregory Desrosiers in his NFL debut or practice squad elevation Phil Mafah, with one game of NFL experience, is anybody's guess.

If you're the Giants, all you can do is cross your fingers and hope the game doesn't turn on a mistake by one of the new, young running backs.

It is never good when your primary kickoff and punt returner shows up on the injury report with a hand injury. That is what happened to Charlie Jones of the Giants this week. When and how the injury occurred I don't know, but it was clear throughout the week that it was a concern. On Thursday, Jones was practicing with a wrap on his hand. He is listed as questionable.

"He's managing it," Harbaugh said. "He was out today catching and everything like that. Just want to make sure he could catch. I haven't talked to him yet. We'll see how he felt."

Starting safety Jevon Holland could return punts if Jones can't.

"Not ideal. If we have to do it, we will. But not ideal," Harbaugh said.

Jones and Tyrone Tracy have been the kickoff returners. Tracy is now on IR with a hamstring injury. Who's next on the depth chart? Good question.

Deonte Banks is an outstanding kickoff returner, but he is also the Giants' best cornerback. Desrosiers returned some kickoffs in college. Jalin Hyatt, just signed to the 53-man roster on Saturday, could be used on kickoff returns. There aren't a lot of other options.

#2729. Warriors keep streak alive, win seventh straight behind Steph Curry's 41 points

SAN FRANCISCO – It wasn't long ago that the Golden State Warriors were being written off, calling the 2026-27 season a throwaway after an 0-3 start.

They've since won seven consecutive games and have slowly become one of the hottest teams in the league. If you were sleeping on Golden State, then it's time to wake up. The boys are balling.

The Warriors kept their win streak intact, battling the Orlando Magic in a 126-119 overtime win on Saturday, Nov. 7 at Chase Center in San Francisco.

The Magic came into the with just two wins and were desperate for a spark. It was an easy situation for the Warriors to overlook. Golden State came out the gates with a 16 point lead but Orlando battled back and made it a game throughout.

"These games always scare me when people are out for the other team (with injury) because the league is filled with hungry, young, athletic players and the way everybody plays now, it's speed, crash the glass, and create extra possessions," Kerr said. "We only got out of there alive because of Steph (Curry) and then some great individual efforts by guys.  We got totally outplayed that whole second half. They were amazing. 33 more field-goal attempts. It's almost impossible to win a game, but I'm proud of our guys, because they gutted it out."

Golden State was led by their veteran superstar Stephen Curry, who scored 12 unanswered points himself in the final 2:21 of regulation en route to a 41-point performance. It was his 16th 40-point game since turning 35 years old. He has the most 40-point games in NBA history by a player age 35 or older.

Curry had a vintage performance in which he gets hot in a flash and becomes unstoppable. He went 13-of-19 from the field, 5-of-10 on 3-point shots and a perfect 10-of-10 at the free throw line. He was the engine for the Warriors, as he's been time and time again throughout his career. It doesn't get old to someone like Draymond Green who's played alongside Curry since 2012.

"It never gets old," Green told USA TODAY Sports. "He's so special, like, he always does something to where it can't get old.  You know, it's always something different. ... Down the stretch, you kind of get to a space where you just expect him to make those plays. But never try to take it for granted."

Green caught himself in awe of Curry on one particular shot when he was being guarded by Magic forward Jamal Cain as the shot clock was winding down with 6:46 left in the third quarter. Cain was all over Curry and still, Curry found space to hoist up a 3-point try and it found the bottom of the net.

"The guy's the greatest shooter ever played basketball. But I don't know what in your mind would just tell you, oh, this guy's pressuring me, just shoot," Green said. "Right? That's crazy. I can't begin to process those thoughts, you know, where you're like, gosh, right here. I'm gonna just shoot it. Most people, they do that and you look at them like, yo, what are you doing? It goes in. So I would say that was the one tonight that was really like, man, it's crazy. But, you know, I try I make it a point to try to never take it for granted."

Curry is going to get his but the battle was won through their depth. Every player who logged minutes for Golden State score. The Warriors bench outscored Orlando's second unit, 42-31.

After Curry, Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had the next high with 23 points on 9-of-15 shooting from the field. Brandin Podziemski added 15 points and 7 rebounds.

The Warriors look to continue their hot streak as they host the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday, Nov. 9 at Chase Center in San Francisco, California. Tip-off begins at 7 p.m. PT (10 p.m. ET).

#2725. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2724. La Liga giants could make move for Chelsea star

Chelsea have a significant decision looming over Levi Colwill, with the club keen to remove any uncertainty around one of the most important defenders in their long-term plans. According to Caught Offside, there is growing interest in the England international from both Liverpool and Barcelona, placing added focus on fresh contract discussions.

Colwill remains tied to Chelsea until 2029, so there is no immediate contractual pressure. Even so, the situation is understood to be one the club would prefer to address well in advance, with new talks viewed internally as a priority heading into 2027. That reflects both his standing at Stamford Bridge and the sense that Chelsea want to prevent a wider transfer issue from developing.

There is a strong belief within Chelsea that Colwill can become a cornerstone of the side for years to come. Having come through the academy, he carries added value on and off the pitch, and the feeling around the club is that he has the profile to become a leader in this project. Injuries may have slowed parts of his progress, but they have not altered the broader view of his importance.

That explains why Chelsea's preference is clear. They want him to stay and would ideally secure that position before external interest gathers further pace. Clubs across Europe monitor elite left-sided defenders closely, and Colwill fits that bracket because of his age, homegrown status, technical quality and ceiling.

Both Liverpool and Barcelona are believed to be attentive to developments. Barcelona's admiration appears especially serious, with one source saying: "Barcelona view Colwill as a top target after studying his performances and stats in great detail. There have been internal discussions about putting a bid together, possibly as early as this January."

Other indications suggest no move is imminent, but Chelsea are understood to be alert to the risk of rival clubs building a relationship with the player's camp before negotiations progress. The plan is for talks in the New Year, by which stage there may be a better sense of whether interest from elsewhere has become more concrete.

Chelsea's position is that Colwill is not for sale, yet market realities always matter. The report suggests intermediaries have floated a valuation in the region of £65m to £75m, a figure that would create a serious internal discussion given Colwill's academy background and the accounting benefits any sale would bring.

One source put it this way: "To be clear, Chelsea want to keep Colwill. That's their plan. But if someone came in with £65-75m they'd have to think about it. Let's see how his contract talks go, but that kind of money would be hard to turn down."

That is where this becomes delicate. Chelsea may see Colwill as part of the future, but an offer at that level would test any resolve, particularly in a market where pure profit sales carry clear appeal.

If the situation were to change, Chelsea are said to admire Como's Jacobo Ramon and AC Milan's Koni De Winter. Jeremy Jacquet had also been tracked before his move to Liverpool. That does not mean Chelsea are planning for life after Colwill, but it does indicate sensible background work as they assess multiple defensive outcomes.

For now, the main task is straightforward. Chelsea need to move decisively, open formal discussions and make sure one of their most valuable young players remains central to the club's defensive future.

This is exactly the kind of story Chelsea cannot allow to drift. Levi Colwill should be one of the untouchables. He is academy developed, already proven at a high level, and still has plenty of room to improve. Players like this are the foundation of a serious team, especially when the squad has already seen so much change in recent years.

The worrying part is that the report makes this sound like a situation that could become vulnerable if not handled properly. Liverpool and Barcelona are not random admirers. If clubs of that stature sense hesitation, they tend to keep pushing and wait for the right opening. Chelsea should not be leaving any room for that.

The mention of £65m to £75m is unsettling as well. Even if that is a huge fee on paper, replacing a left-sided defender with Colwill's profile, homegrown status and connection to the club would be far more difficult than balancing a set of accounts. Selling him would send the wrong message about what this project is meant to be.

If Chelsea genuinely believe Colwill can become a leader, then the next step is obvious. Get the talks done, show him he is central to the future, and remove the noise before it turns into a saga that drags on for months.

#2722. Kenny Atkinson takes jokes as lesson for ‘analytically’ comment in last season’s playoff loss to Knicks

CLEVELAND — Kenny Atkinson has been getting mocked for months. The jokes at the Cavaliers coach's expense — courtesy of Josh Hart, Karl-Anthony Towns and countless others — could continue for years to come.

After losing the first three games of the Eastern Conference finals, Atkinson infamously said that the Cavaliers had "analytically" won two of the first three games against the Knicks, but the Long Island native wishes the question that prompted his comment — regarding what hope the Cavaliers had of becoming the first NBA team to overcome a 3-0 series deficit — had as long a lifespan.

"When you take the context of the question, I'm not sure that was taken into account, that's a little bit of a lesson for me, you can just take a sound bite," Atkinson said.

"There was no coach more complimentary of the Knicks and honest about our performance and how they dominated us … 99 percent of my comments were how they dominated us. They were by far the better team."

Even if some of the numbers were on Cleveland's side, Atkinson acknowledges that so much of the difference in the lopsided series couldn't be measured.

Kenny Atkinson reacts during the Knicks' 109-97 win over the Cavaliers on Nov. 7, 2026 in Cleveland. Getty Images

"There's the mental toughness, the physical toughness, how aggressive you are, all these other intangibles that go into that," Atkinson said. "In no sense was it like, 'Oh man, we deserve to be winning.' There was zero thought of that."

The Knicks traveled without Hart, who missed his second consecutive game due to right ankle soreness despite practicing with the team the previous day in New York.

The Knicks have not set a timetable for Hart's return, but coach Mike Brown expressed no long-term concern, noting that the team's schedule — featuring one game in a five-day span — played a role in giving Hart additional time to recover.

"It's nothing major," Brown said. "He did go through some of practice [Friday]. I set him out of some contact, so we just want to take advantage where we are schedule-wise."

Brown named Andre Drummond the Knicks' best defensive player in the 109-97 win.

The backup big man had eight rebounds, two steals and one block in 14 minutes

Jose Alvarado recorded a DNP-CD, while Tyler Kolek backed up Jalen Brunson, finishing with five assists, four rebounds and one steal in 14 minutes

Jordan Clarkson shot 4-for-5, finishing with nine points and two offensive rebounds. … Mikal Bridges' shooting struggles continued, as he shot just 1-for-7 on 3-pointers, finishing with nine points. … The Knicks held a 26-8 edge in second-chance points.

Hart, who missed eight games last season with a right ankle injury, also missed the team's preseason finale Oct. 15 due to the same issue. The 31-year-old started each of the team's first seven games of the season, most recently suiting up in Monday's win against the Nets. He is averaging 8.6 points — his fewest in eight years — while shooting a career-worst 38.6 percent from the field.

Landry Shamet, who scored nine points, made his second consecutive start in Hart's place.

#2721. Brandon Aiyuk potential landing spots: Where might the WR play next?

There is a wide range of speculation that wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk will likely not play for the San Francisco 49ers.

Niners general manager John Lynch indicated that Aiyuk had more than likely played his "last snap" for San Francisco earlier this year in January.

Aiyuk made a number of social media posts that ridiculed the 49ers in cryptic captions as he finally broke his silence. San Francisco continued to ignore Aiyuk's antics and addressed its need to fill depth at the wide receiver position.

The 49ers signed Mike Evans, Christian Kirk, Deebo Samuel Sr. and a number of other receivers, even selecting Ole Miss star wideout De'Zhaun Stribling with the 33rd overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. San Francisco has long indicated they are done with the Aiyuk show.

Aiyuk had a meeting with the 49ers' front office, who he described as the "big bosses" to reporters. Aiyuk signed star agent Drew Rosenhaus in an attempt to get back into the league. Aiyuk must first be reinstated and repay $13 million in bonus forfeiture pay.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy in my recovery process, in my rehab process," Aiyuk said. "(I'm) back to 100% and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League."

Rosenhaus didn't have much to comment regarding their meeting with the Niners.

As those conversations continue, or stall out, which of the other NFL teams could utilize the skillset that Aiyuk can bring? Here are potential landing spots for the wide receiver:

The Ravens don't have a lot of weapons at the wideout position, but they do have Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman. Regardless of who they have, does it matter considering who they don't have? Quarterback Lamar Jackson is out indefinitely with a right thumb injury. As a backup, they traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett. Maybe Aiyuk could be a viable option as the Ravens look to salvage their season.

The Raiders are an interesting option. They are known for being a place for second chances for players. The franchise is in need of a true No. 1 option at wide receiver. They've been getting away with Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor as their main wideout options. They have tight end Brock Bowers, who they utilize and target as if he's a WR1. Aiyuk would thrive in silver and black catching passes from Kirk Cousins.

Titans quarterback Cam Ward needs additional weapons beyond starters Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley. Aiyuk would be a veteran presence for the Titans' young receiver core. The season hasn't gone the way they'd hope, but maybe the 28-year-old could come in and help build on the season and look forward to 2027.

Aaron Rodgers is on his last leg and adding Aiyuk could be the missing piece that the Steelers need. They have been trying to sharpen the DK Metcalf connection with Rodgers. Aiyuk could be the latest weapon for Rodgers in the twilight of his career.

The Seahawks make an interesting possibility simply because it's a division rival and Aiyuk would have a chance to face the 49ers before the season ends if a trade were to be finalized before the Nov. 10 deadline. It's hard to imagine a world in which the Niners send Aiyuk to a rival, but maybe they want him to be their headache. However, Aiyuk seems like the guy that would take it personal next time he sees San Francisco, how fitting would it be.

This one seems the most far off, but not really. It's not likely that San Francisco would do anything that could potentially help the Chiefs, but Aiyuk would be a perfect fit with quarterback Patrick Mahomes. The Chiefs are also known for reviving careers, but of course, winning helps. Aiyuk, if healthy, certainly helps their WR room. He would join Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen.

#2718. Diving deeper into Cavs 109-97 loss to Knicks: The more things change, the more they stay the same

CLEVELAND — The Cleveland Cavaliers couldn't keep up with a New York Knicks team that just has their number. They dropped Saturday's game 109-97.

Brunson is a certified Cavs killer. He picked up right where he left off last postseason by torching whatever defender Cleveland put in front of him. He got inside the paint and to his midrange floater with ease. And when he didn't, the outside shot was working as well.

There really isn't much that you can do when Brunson has it going as he did here. The Cavs sent some doubles at him and tried to shade their defense toward him. When they got too far, he made the easy pass to the open teammate, never forcing anything.

The Cavs' strategy was fine. The defense also wasn't necessarily horrible. Cleveland's guards competed, but that didn't matter. Brunson is just too good a shot and decision-maker.

37 points, 4 assists, 4 rebounds, 2 steals, 1 block

Mitchell is putting together an impressive season from a process standpoint. He's doing a better job of looking for his teammates, while also finding avenues to score.

"I think the biggest thing is creating an opportunity," Mitchell said. "I haven't shot as many shots as I have in my career, so trying to balance that and figure out trying to make the right basketball play. Sometimes that is shooting. Sometimes that is passing. Sometimes that is running the blitz, and it's going to help to make me better."

Mitchell tried to will the Cavs back into this game, scoring 21 in the final quarter alone. But as impressive as he was, a one-man army wasn't enough to take down a well-oiled machine like the Knicks. Especially when the rest of his co-stars struggled.

Anything bought from the links helps support Fear the Sword. You can buy the Spida shirt HERE. You can also shop all of Homage's Cavs gear HERE.

29 points, 13 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 steals

Towns is such a difficult player to defend. His outside shot requires him to be guarded out on the perimeter, which opens up the lane for his teammates. If the defensive center leaves, Towns can make them pay with the outside shot. And, if his defender closes out too hard, Towns is quick enough off the dribble to make them pay inside.

This was on display on Saturday. He drew two quick fouls on Mobley in the first quarter by attacking the rim. This changed the complexion of the game. Without Jarrett Allen, the Cavs were forced to turn to third-string center Thomas Bryant for a longer stretch than they would've ideally liked.

Towns's presence can completely change an offense as dynamic as New York's. Cleveland found that out again the hard way.

7 points on 2-of-9 shooting, 5 assists, 2 rebounds, 2 blocks

The Cavs offense can look lifeless when Harden isn't able to get downhill. On Saturday, he was a step slow and couldn't create any separation off the dribble. That limited his effectiveness.

On the other end, the Knicks continually hunted him in mismatches. To his credit, Harden competed. But it wasn't enough to keep this from being a winning strategy.

This has been less than an ideal start to the season for Harden.

12 points, 9 rebounds, 5 assists, 3 turnovers

Mobley's ability to win the matchup over Joel Embiid was a deciding factor in Cleveland's runaway win over the Philadelphia 76ers. Likewise, his inability to do so against New York contributed to the loss.

The foul trouble made it difficult for Mobley to establish any kind of offense inside. This left him as mostly a jump shooter at the start of the game. And since the three-ball wasn't falling (1-for-5 on the evening), there wasn't much he was capable of offensively to help jumpstart an offense that needed it.

Watson was useful in this game. He provided some much-needed offense and was helpful as a defender. That's what you want to see from Watson in this matchup.

"Not really. In Jauary we went 2-9. I'm not really into measuring stick games). … Let's say we win by 15. Well, we might get hammered next week by whoever's in last place by 20. Does that mean we suck? No. You just take it one game at a time and try to get a little bit better."

– Knicks head coach Mike Brown before the game when asked if this was a measuring stick game

It's tempting to use this difficult stretch of games as a test for where the Cavs are. And if you were going to use it as one, they wouldn't necessarily pass.

The more concerning thing is the lack of discernible identity. When they're playing well, the Cavs can beat anyone, as we saw against Philadelphia. But what does this group hang their hat on? What does better look like for them? And are they taking steps to get there? Those are the questions that matter, and we don't have clear answers for any of them.

The Knicks outscored the Cavs 26-8 in second-chance points.

New York retrieved 41.8% of their missed shots (94th percentile). And then they made the most of those opportunities by scoring a quarter's worth of points on that alone.

"We have to rebound better collectively," head coach Kenny Atkinson said. "There's no one pointing the finger. The guys got to do it collectively. We just got to be better."

I don't necessarily think the Knicks present stylistic problems that the Cavs can't solve. An offense that hunts out mismatches with their smaller, but electric, scoring guard isn't something the Cavs should, on paper, be incapable of countering. Yet, the Cavs are consistently ending up on the wrong side of this matchup. The Knicks have their number, and there's no way around that.

Atkinson and Mitchell were asked what makes this matchup so difficult afterward. Both pointed to the offensive rebounding as an obvious issue, and one that we all can see. They also both mentioned that the Knicks just understand how to play with each other and use that to seize the openings teams give them.

"They really have solutions," Atkinson said. "I think their continuity…they just have great chemistry. They're on a string on both ends."

"They've been through stuff together as a group," Mitchell said. "They do a good job os seizing mistakes."

Brunson and Towns were tremendous once again tonight. Their shotmaking carried them in this matchup. But they also did a great job of accepting what the Cavs threw at them, and then having a plan of action for that. If you doubled Brunson, he moved the ball to the open teammate and made the Cavs' defense scramble out.

Conversely, when they threw doubles at Mitchell, the Cavs weren't quick to respond. Watson admitted afterward that he doesn't know to help Mitchell in that situation and that there are "some questions" about their strategy that he would like to ask about. That isn't the sign of a team that's on a string and understands what they need to do to be the best version of themselves.

Little things like that are why the Knicks have been better. They understand what they need to do, and the pieces fit together perfectly to make that happen. The Cavs don't have that right now. And until they do, they won't be able to get through the roadblock the Knicks have become throughout this era of Cavs basketball.

#2716. Eagles vs. Giants Week 9 game information

The Philadelphia Eagles are now 2-6 heading into their Week 9 matchup against the New York Giants, and will now turn to their fourth starting quarterback of the season — Joe Mixon.

Offensively, the Eagles have done some decent, albeit incredibly inconsistent, things over the past few weeks, but injuries have still made it a losing battle, and they've failed to adjust to their current roster. They only gave Tanner McKee three weeks to try and get comfortable in this new offense before benching him earlier this week for Joe Mixon. Mixon was signed by the Eagles off the Cowboys practice squad just three weeks ago.

Head coach Nick Sirianni spoke about the decision a few days ago, explaining that they feel confident in Mixon's ability and athleticism, and ultimately, they felt he gave the team a better chance moving forward. The QB will likely have Saquon Barkley to help alleviate some pressure, but they are still without DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks for this game. Fortunately, the young wide outs have shown a lot of potential, but they need someone to get them the ball — and according to reports, Mixon is a guy who will get them the ball with speed and strength.

#2715. RBL light it up against Augsburg to continue stunning home run

"We need to make that mental switch," RBL head coach Martín Demichelis had sagely insisted ahead of the game. Following on from our fourth midweek fixture in a row, the energy-sapping 3-2 defeat to Manchester City, FC Augsburg presented a very different challenge.

Indeed, another wake-up call came almost immediately after kick-off. Just 37 seconds in, a defensive clearance from none other than captain Willi Orbán went horribly wrong - on his 400th competitive appearance for RBL, mind. Within the first minute of the Bundesliga fixture, Leipzig were already behind.

"In 400 games, I've never started a match as badly as I did today. But perhaps it was meant to be," Willi explained. "After that, I quickly felt good again because we did a superb job."

On the pitch, the RBL legend and his teammates produced the perfect response to the early setback. It was a fittingly special afternoon for the Hungary international, who received a standing ovation both when he was substituted and again at full-time.

Enjoying around 70 percent of possession, the Red Bulls gradually took control of the game and turned it around before half-time. Three goals in the space of just 12 minutes put us firmly in the driving seat, including a beauty of a free kick from David Raum.

"I really liked the way we stuck to our ethos on the pitch despite conceding so early," Micho said, full of praise for his players.

The game plan initially placed a clear emphasis on the right flank, with Brajan Gruda well and truly in the thick of it against FCA. His mazing runs into the box repeatedly drew two or three Augsburg defenders towards him, creating space for Ezechiel Banzuzi and Christopher Nkunku to score our first and second goals respectively. With five chances created, Brajan was the most creative player on the pitch.

The winger, who has once again been called up to the Germany squad, received praise from several quarters. "Brajan's performance was outstanding," said Micho. Raumi described it as a "brilliant performance", which was duly recognised with the Man of the Match award.

"I played the way I always play. A lot of things came off for me today. I think dribbling is simply in my blood. I had so much fun out there," Brajan reflected after his outstanding display.

Across Europe's top five leagues, the left-footer has completed more successful dribbles per 90 minutes than any other player (6.1), ahead of former Leipzig man Yan Diomande (4.4) and Lamine Yamal (4.3)!

After the break, Augsburg managed to keep Brajan a little quieter, but we showcased our dynamism and versatility and continued to come up with good ideas on the ball. We struck twice from the left during a spell of pressure from the visitors.

A late Augsburg consolation to make it 5-2 did little to take the shine off a convincing home victory. With 23 goals scored in our first five home games, we have equalled Bayern Munich's Bundesliga record from the 2023/24 season. The results are there to back it up too - we have now won ten consecutive Bundesliga home games across two seasons. "There's no stopping us at home!" was how Willi summed it up.

The bigger picture is looking positive as well. The team's philosophy looks clearer week after week, with their determination and passion on full display, as well as a clear hunger to score even more goals. Meanwhile, more and more players are hitting their stride. Alongside Brajan, Rômulo is another player in outstanding form. The Brazilian forward has found the net four times in his last three Bundesliga appearances.

With 18 points, we remain hot on the heels of the teams above us, with Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund both on 21 points.

Weiter geht es am 21. November mit dem Auswärtsspiel bei Union Berlin. Zuvor sind viele unserer Jungs mit ihren Nationalteams unterwegs. „Es bleibt bis Weihnachten eine intensive Zeit", blickt Willi voraus. Drei weitere Englische Wochen warten auf uns. Wir haben Bock! Our next fixture comes on 21st November, when we travel to Union Berlin. Before then, many of our players will be away on international duty. "It's going to be an intense period right through to Christmas," Willi predicted. "We've got another three midweek fixtures coming up. We're ready for it!"

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

Rookie Porter Martone asserted himself as a budding star with six goals and nine assists in 19 games between the regular season and playoffs.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.

#2713. Erik Spoelstra Shrugs Off Doc Rivers’ Critique of Giannis Antetokounmpo

On Thursday's episode of "The Bill Simmons Podcast," former Milwaukee Bucks coach Doc Rivers made some eyebrow-raising comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo. According to Rivers, Antetokounmpo is "a difficult guy" to coach, and his lack of "super IQ" on the basketball court curtails his athleticism and passing ability.

This season, Antetokounmpo is under the tutelage of Erik Spoelstra as he suits up for the Miami Heat. In an interview with The Athletic's Eric Nehm, Spoelstra acknowledged Rivers' remarks.

"Look, I like Doc, and I respect him, this is our business now. We went into the season thinking that that would be a process, playing with somebody (Giannis) that commands so much attention. That's a different style than some of the guys that have come here, that have played before. We'll be able to figure that all out."

Spoelstra, who is in his 19th season as the Heat's coach, added that his team has responded well to his messaging.

"We've already made a lot of strides. I'm on this mountaintop pounding my fist, and our guys understand it."

With Antetokounmpo in the fold, Miami dropped its first four games and now faces the difficult task of overcoming a 3-6 start.

Integrating Antetokounmpo into the grand scheme of things has been a top priority for Spoelstra and his staff. Fortunately for the Heat, the team has plenty of time to learn how to maximize Antetokounmpo's skill set this season.

As for player-turned-analyst Antonio Daniels, Rivers isn't necessarily wrong in his assessment of Giannis Antetokounmpo's abilities.

Appearing on SiriusXM NBA Radio on Friday, Daniels (a 14-year NBA pro who now works as a New Orleans Pelicans color analyst) broke down the nuances of Rivers' comments.

"He's not wrong, but the timing is wrong…Because Doc Rivers is now retired from coaching and Giannis is no longer in Milwaukee. If this was said 3 or 4 years ago down the line, I get it."

Daniels added that the shortcomings Rivers pointed out don't diminish Antetokounmpo's "greatness," arguing that it's possible to be a great player while also being "difficult to play with."

The meeting presents an important opportunity for both sides to strengthen their positions in the 2. Bundesliga table as the season progresses. Bochum will be looking to make home advantage count, while Karlsruher SC travel to North Rhine-Westphalia hoping to come away with a positive result.

Bochum head into Sunday's encounter with renewed confidence after ending their difficult run of league form with a 2-1 victory away to Energie Cottbus last weekend.

Uwe Rösler's side had endured a five-game winless run in the league before travelling to Cottbus, but Christian Rasmussen's late winner secured three valuable points and lifted the club to 11th in the standings.

The victory was particularly important given Bochum's struggles in front of goal this season. Having scored just eight times in their opening ten league matches, they currently possess the lowest-scoring attack in the division. However, their recent cup victory over Mainz and the comeback success against Cottbus suggest that Rösler's team are beginning to find some momentum.

Rösler is nevertheless expecting a difficult afternoon against a Karlsruhe side whose intensity and attacking movement could cause problems. Speaking ahead of the fixture, the Bochum coach described Sunday's encounter as a potential 50-50 contest and warned that the visitors are one of the most intense teams in the division.

The German side will need to pay particular attention to Marvin Wanitzek, who Rösler identified as Karlsruhe's standout player, highlighting his ability to find space and influence matches through both open play and set-pieces.

Karlsruher SC travel to Bochum looking to build on an encouraging 2-1 victory over 1. FC Heidenheim, which brought some much-needed stability to their start under new head coach Maximilian Senft.

The Baden-Württemberg outfit had endured a difficult spell before welcoming Heidenheim, having suffered a heavy 6-1 defeat away to Magdeburg immediately after an impressive 4-0 home victory against Darmstadt.

However, goals from Tim Civeja and Marvin Wanitzek secured a deserved victory over the recently-relegated side last weekend, with Wanitzek's superb free-kick proving decisive.

Despite that result, consistency remains a significant concern for Senft. Karlsruhe have collected 11 points from their opening ten league matches, leaving them level with Bochum, although their inferior goal difference places them two positions below Sunday's opponents.

Their away form is another area requiring improvement, with the visitors yet to record an away victory in the league this season, collecting just two points from their four matches on the road.

Senft acknowledged that his team must become more consistent when discussing their recent performances, explaining that the squad are still developing under his new tactical approach.

"We are coming out of the Heidenheim game strengthened, particularly because of the way we performed tactically and mentally," the Austrian coach explained. He also stressed his desire to deliver positive performances more frequently rather than continuing to experience such significant fluctuations.

Karlsruhe will therefore be hoping that last weekend's victory can provide the platform for a more convincing away performance, particularly against a Bochum side who have also struggled to find consistency this season.

Historically, Bochum have enjoyed the better of this fixture, recording 23 victories compared to Karlsruhe's 16 across 64 competitive meetings, with the remaining 25 encounters ending in draws.

However, the more recent record at the Vonovia Ruhrstadion offers encouragement for the visitors. Karlsruhe have avoided defeat on each of their last six visits to Bochum, who have not beaten them at home since a 1-0 victory in May 2014.

Interestingly, 13 of the 24 meetings between the sides in the 2. Bundesliga have ended in draws, highlighting how closely contested this fixture has traditionally been.

The previous meeting came on the final day of the 2025/26 campaign, when Bochum claimed a 2-1 away victory thanks to Moritz-Broni Kwarteng's winning goal.

Bochum will be without several players for Sunday's encounter, with Enis Cokaj, Jean Manuel Mbom and Oliver Olsen having returned to training but not yet being available for selection.

Babis Drakas and Philipp Strompf are also not ready to return, while Berkan Taz missed one training session earlier in the week. However, Rösler confirmed that the remainder of his squad had completed full training.

The Bochum coach also suggested that changes could be made to his attacking partnership, with Philipp Hofmann having played a significant number of minutes recently. Charlie Patiño and Jarne Steuckers are among those pushing for starting opportunities following encouraging substitute appearances.

Karlsruhe, meanwhile, will again be without defensive regulars Marcel Franke and Sebastian Jung, who are both unavailable through injury.

New signing Héliton has completed his first full week of training since the previous international break, although Senft indicated that he is more likely to be considered for a brief appearance rather than a starting role.

Paul Scholl is consequently expected to retain his place in the back three after impressing during the 2-1 victory over Heidenheim, while Tim Civeja will also hope to keep his place following his first goal in the second division.

VfL Bochum (4-2-3-1): Horn; Klaiber, Steinwender, Mets, Wittek; Pannewig, Meyer; Taz, Rasmussen, Miyoshi; Hofmann

Karlsruher SC (3-4-2-1): Bernat; Kobald, Scholl, Trémoulet; Pinto Pedrosa, Väänänen, Civeja, Ofli; Wiethaup, Wanitzek; Fukuda

#2710. Yaxel Lendeborg continues to revive a Warriors team everyone left for dead

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Warriors fans are losing their collective mind over Yaxel Lendeborg, who continued to one-up himself on Sunday in leading Golden State to a win over the Clippers without Stephen Curry and Draymond Green. It was a completely outrageous performance: 37 points in 34 minutes on 68% shooting, including six 3-pointers.

The rookie added six assists. Threw in four boards and a steal for fun. What this guy has done over his first two NBA weeks is almost beyond comprehension. We're talking about the only rookie in NBA history other than Larry Bird to card at least 100 points, 40 rebounds and 20 assists through his first five games.

His sixth career game was his lone stinker. Luka Dončić gave him a proper hazing. But Lendeborg got right back on the horse on Sunday to become the fourth rookie in history to post 37 and five in a single game on 85% true shooting. Those 37 points are the most scored in a single game by a Warriors rookie since Curry had 42 in 2010, and Lendeborg now ranks as just the third Warriors rookie to average north of 20 PPG (22.3) over the first seven games of his career. The other two are Wilt Chamberlain and Rick Barry. Not bad company.

Yaxel Lendeborg scored 37 points to lead Golden State to victory, the most by a Warriors rookie in a game since Stephen Curry had 42 in 2010.Lendeborg is averaging 22.3 PPG this season, he's the 3rd player in Warriors history to average 20 PPG over his first 7 career games,… pic.twitter.com/T3RgsjFPB9

"That was a huge letdown last game," Lendeborg said of putting his foot in his mouth against the Lakers during his postgame interview. "I just try not to be a letdown again, honestly. I know I've got to keep my confidence no matter what goes on, good or bad game. And I just got to start playing with the joy that I played with the last six years of college and now here. So I'm just continuing to try to keep playing with a smile on my face, maybe throw a little dance move like Steph every once in a while. But I'm gonna just keep trying to find my joy."

Joy is an understatement. This dude's got Dub Nation flying. When I was growing up, there was a great song by Garth Brooks called "Unanswered Prayers," and I thought of it on Sunday as I watched Yaxel burying shot after shot from just about every spot and in every fashion possible, because I'll tell you this: a lot of Warriors fans are thanking the basketball gods that their pissed-off prayers to trade this summer's No. 11 pick fell on Dunleavy's deaf ears.

I mean, look at this guy, in his second week as a pro, chewing the Clippers up like a total 1A alpha.

Yaxel Lendeborg in win vs. Clippers:37 PTS6 AST4 REB13-19 FG6-11 3PTMost points in a game by a Warriors rookie since Stephen Curry in 2010.pic.twitter.com/rSIyjqIEmW

"He's playing this way and he really doesn't know the NBA game yet," Warriors coach Steve Kerr said after Sunday's game. "The game is still really fast for him, but he's so skilled and so talented that he's making all kinds of plays out there. It's remarkable the impact he's having on these games in the first couple weeks of the season."

Look at that reel. This is a rookie who played in just 11 high school games and had to start his career at a junior college taking over an NBA court like a coporate raider. Let's start with the one-on-one scoring, which he's doing in every manner possible: Bullying defenders in the paint, going by them off the dribble, pulling up from 3. Look at these isolation metrics from Tim Legler's All-NBA podcast:

This wasn't just a one-game thing, which, if you've actually been watching and have a functional pair of eyes, you already know. But the numbers are still startling. As further pointed out by the All-NBA pod, Lendeborg is currently the most efficient isolation scorer in the league at 1.52 points per direct play.

When he's not scoring one on one, Yaxel is running the floor like a Hummer or drawing two and dishing. With Curry out, he served as Golden State's point guard, which he noted afterward he's "always wanted to be." He calmed possessions like a veteran. Toggled between pick-and-roll handler and screener. Yaxel did al this while committing just two turnovers, which, during what has otherwise been an almost perfect first NBA impression, has registered as a lone hiccup.

But we have to get back to the shooting. Specifically, the pull-up shooting from range. It's one thing for a guy his size to be a spot-up threat, but this stuff off the dribble, in Kerr's words, "changes everything" in terms of Yaxel's potential.

"We knew he was a good shooter," Kerr said. "When he came in to work out, you could see the skill in terms of being able to put it on the floor and pull up and shoot, but I didn't expect what I saw tonight."

Frankly, you can remove the "tonight" from that answer. Anyone who says they expected anything close to what we've seen from Lendeborg at any point over these first seven games is a stone-cold liar. This dude is giving life to an old, decaying team that everyone left for dead this summer, and certainly after starting the year 0-3. The energy after four straight wins is undeniable. And now you have to wonder if the Warriors' front office has a mind to get aggressive on the trade market rather than waiting for their cap space to open this summer.

Because the simple truth is that Curry remains the best player in the world on any given night. Maybe that fact alone wasn't enough to justify putting the pedal down on this season before Yaxel emerged as a total beast, but now that he has, and with Jimmy Butler set to come back some time after the first of the year, this is a team that can really compete with another piece. They have the Draymond Green and Kristaps Porzingis contracts. They have the draft capital. They have Butler on an expiring deal if they want to go that route. The only question is, do they have the nerve?

#2708. Luka Dončić explains his 'step forward' on defense after five-steal performance vs. Raptors

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić currently leads the NBA in scoring by an astounding 8.1 points per game, as his 37.7 ppg average dwarfs Tyrese Maxey's 29.6 ppg in second place.

On Sunday night, Dončić increased that average with 45 points (along with 15 rebounds and six assists) in a 131-125 win over the Toronto Raptors, but after the game, much of the focus was on what Dončić did on the defensive end of the floor. Since he entered the league, no one has confused Dončić with an elite defender, but through six games this season, a leaner Luka has looked more engaged and improved on the defensive end for the Lakers.

Sunday night was his best statistical performance yet, as he produced five steals and drew three charges against the Raptors to give the Lakers eight extra possessions that became critical in a six-point win. That effort offered a proof point for Dončić of what he views as a genuine step forward he's taken on defense in his ninth season in the NBA.

"Obviously, I'm not the best defender in the NBA, but I think this year, I really took a step forward," Dončić said (via ESPN). "Obviously, people are going to talk what they want to talk [about] me. ... But I know, and my team knows, that I'm better this year."

Those three charges drawn now tie him for the most in the league this season, alongside Aaron Nesmith, Davion Mitchell, Draymond Green, Jalen Brunson and Keyonte George. He's averaging 1.8 steals per game, which is tied for 15th in the league, and while many will be quick to point out that charges and steals aren't necessarily a sign of great defense, they do point to Dončić's effort level being raised on that end of the floor.

For years, Dončić has been viewed as a one-way player. He is one of the elite offensive engines in the NBA, up in the tier with Nikola Jokić and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for the title of best in the world. Defense has never been his calling card, and much of the frustration with Dončić's conditioning is due to a lack of effort on that end of the floor.

This year, Dončić seems to have bought into the importance of showing stronger effort on defense as he takes the reins as the Lakers' leader with the departure of LeBron James. Lakers coach J.J. Redick sees Dončić taking charges as him proving he's taking a step forward as a leader as much as anything.

"I think taking a charge in general is just a form of leadership, right? You're putting your body on the line for the team," Redick said. "... He's trying to win. You see the competitiveness come out so many times on the offensive end, but he's competitive on the defensive end, too."

Between Dončić and Austin Reaves, the Lakers have the potential to be one of the league's elite offensive units. The question coming into the season was whether they could do enough defensively to hold up with a roster that doesn't feature many high-end defenders outside of Walker Kessler.

Through seven games, the Lakers rank 20th in the NBA in defensive rating (113.9). While that's just a bit below league average, for a team with the second-best offensive rating in the league (119.9), it's enough to get the job done. The concern for the Lakers is whether Dončić and the rest will be able to maintain that effort level on defense as the season wears on.

It's easy to commit on the defensive end for a couple weeks coming out of camp, but it's much harder to be locked in 50 games into the season. The Lakers being 20th in the league in defense while touting Dončić's improvement on that end and an increased effort level suggests that if that commitment wanes from Dončić and others, their defense could crash closer to the league's worst units. That would negate the advantage they gain with an elite offense and bring them down a tier in terms of being a contender.

That will be worth monitoring as the season progresses, but for now Dončić and the Lakers are getting a proof point of what they can do when they're locked in defensively. Perhaps most importantly, Dončić is seeing that he can still be an elite offensive player while putting a bit more into his defense, which may make it easier for him to stay committed on the defensive side all year.

For the Lakers to be a threat in the West, the offense has to be elite but the defense needs to simply be serviceable. For now, they've figured out that formula, thanks in part to their star buying in and trying to lead by example with an increased focus on doing the right things defensively.

#2707. MLB qualifying offer: Predicting who will get a QO this offseason, plus how the $23.15 million contract works

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Milwaukee Brewers have been crowned the 2026 World Series champions and the 2026-27 offseason is already underway. More than 100 players became free agents the day after the World Series ended, and soon teams will have to make decisions about contract options and qualifying offers.

The qualifying offer (QO) entitles teams to draft-pick compensation in the event that they lose a free agent to another team. The QO is a one-year deal set at the average of the top 125 salaries in baseball. This offseason, it's worth a record $23.15 million, according to the New York Post. That is up from $22.025 million last year, $21.05 million the year before, and $20.325 million the year before that.

Teams have until five days after the end of the World Series to tender their free agents the QO, and players who receive it then have until 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 17 to accept or reject. Players who accept the QO remain with their team and cannot be traded without their consent until June 15. Players who reject the QO become free agents with draft-pick compensation attached.

Simple, right? The process is, but the decisions aren't always. With that in mind, let's run down this offseason's QO candidates, as well as explain the draft-pick compensation rules.

Yes, the QO is still a thing this offseason. The collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and the next CBA could change the QO rules, maybe even eliminate it entirely. That said, until that happens, the QO remains in place. Decisions to tender the QO (made by the team) and decisions to accept or reject the QO (made by the player) are due before the CBA expires.

Once upon a time, teams that lost an eligible free agent received a compensation draft pick after the first round. It was nice and easy. The current rules are a bit more complicated. Here are compensation rules for teams that lose a qualified free agent:

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round)

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round)

The Athletics, Brewers, Cardinals, Diamondbacks, Guardians, Mariners, Marlins, Orioles, Pirates, Rays, Reds, Rockies, Royals, Tigers, and Twins received revenue sharing this season, so the first two scenarios apply to them. The Blue Jays, Braves, Cubs, Dodgers, Mets, Padres, Phillies, Red Sox, and Yankees will pay competitive balance tax (CBT), so they're in the third scenario. The Angels, Astros, Giants, Nationals, Rangers, and White Sox neither received revenue sharing nor paid CBT. They're in the fourth bucket.

Now here are the penalties for signing a qualified free agent:

The Blue Jays, Braves, Cubs, Dodgers, Mets, Padres, Phillies, Red Sox, and Yankees will pay CBT and are in the first group. The Athletics, Brewers, Cardinals, Diamondbacks, Guardians, Mariners, Marlins, Orioles, Pirates, Rays, Reds, Rockies, Royals, Tigers, and Twins received revenue sharing and are in the second group. The Angels, Astros, Giants, Nationals, Rangers, and White Sox are the third group. Got it? Good.

Thirteen players received the QO last offseason: Trent Grisham, Shota Imanaga, Gleyber Torres, and Brandon Woodruff accepted the QO; Zac Gallen, Michael King, and Kyle Schwarber declined but signed new contracts to remain with their teams; Bo Bichette, Dylan Cease, Edwin Díaz, Kyle Tucker, Ranger Suárez, and Framber Valdez rejected the QO and signed with new teams, giving their former clubs compensatory draft picks. Teams do not gain or lose draft picks for re-signing their own qualified free agent.

Players are eligible for the QO as long as they spent the entire 2026 season with one team and did not receive the QO previously. That means several high-profile free agents are not eligible for the QO this offseason. Here are the notables:

CHANGED TEAMS Luis Arraez Kevin Gausman (also received QO previously) Casey Mize Freddy Peralta Tarik Skubal Daulton Varsho

PREVIOUSLY RECEIVED QO Bo Bichette (opt out) Sonny Gray (mutual option) Michael King (opt out)  Nick Martinez

The Tigers traded Skubal, the reigning two-time AL Cy Young winner, to the Dodgers for a three-prospect package at the deadline. MLB Pipeline currently ranks those players as Detroit's No. 1 (Zyhir Hope), No. 3 (River Ryan), and No. 9 (Brady Smith) prospects. That's a much better haul than the compensation draft pick the Tigers would have received had they kept Skubal all year and made him the QO. Anyway, these free agents are among those not eligible for the QO this offseason.

This is not the best free agent class and, as a result, I count only two stone-cold locks to receive a QO: Randy Arozarena (Mariners) and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs). The Mariners and Cubs would be thrilled if Arozarena and Seiya accepted the QO and returned next season on one-year contracts that aren't too much of a raise. Arozarena made $15.65 million this year. Suzuki earned $18 million. The jump to $23.15 million isn't big enough to shy away from the QO, plus these are really good players. Arozarena and Suzuki will receive the QO and decline it.

Although Arozarena and Suzuki are the only locks to get the QO, in my opinion, there are three other free agents-to-be who seem like pretty good bets to receive it. Here are those three players:

Ryan Jeffers, Twins: Jeffers will be the best catcher to hit the open market since Willson Contreras four years ago. He missed time with a hamate injury this year and his defense isn't great, plus he'll turn 30 next June. Those seem like nitpicks compared to the offense he brings to the table at the catcher position. The only reason I don't think Jeffers is a lock to get the QO is the fact that the Twins have shaved roughly $50 million off their payroll the last four years. They might get thrifty.

Brandon Lowe, Pirates: Pittsburgh knocked it out of the park with the Mike Burrows-for-Lowe-and-Mason Montgomery three-team trade with the Astros and Rays. Montgomery is a bullpen ace and Lowe slugged 35 home runs, the most by a Pirate since Josh Bell hit 37 in 2019. Lowe's age (32), poor contact rates, and history of poor defense (though not in 2026) create collapse risk. Also, the Pirates run a bottom 10 payroll every season. I expect Lowe to get the QO. I just wouldn't be surprised if the Pirates decide not to risk him taking it, thereby soaking up 20% or so of their 2027 payroll.

Trevor Rogers, Orioles: Rogers, 29 in November, was a bright spot in an otherwise lost season for the O's. He stayed healthy and threw a career-high 169 ⅔ innings, and pitched exceptionally well after June 1: 2.90 ERA with under-the-hood numbers to match (2.89 FIP and 3.10 expected ERA). Rogers might be the second-best free agent starter behind Skubal given his success the last two years and (more importantly) analytically friendly arsenal. During the president of baseball operations Mike Elias era, the Orioles haven't always done the most sensible thing when it comes to spending money. I think it's 99% certain the O's will give Rogers the QO, but 99% is not 100%.

My hunch is teams will be conservative with their QO decisions this offseason because a new CBA is coming, and no one knows what the game's economic landscape will look like next year. Will there be a salary cap? More punitive CBT penalties? I would expect teams to err on the side of caution when it comes to potentially committing $23.15 million to one player. Even a good player they may want back, but not necessarily at $23.15 million in 2027. Here are three borderline QO cases:

David Bednar, Yankees: Bednar has proven he can close games in New York, which is not nothing, but he did just turn 32, and the $23.15 million QO would make him the highest-paid reliever in baseball. I think the Yankees want to bring Bednar back next season. Enough to risk him accepting the QO? When the potential reward is a dinky draft pick after the fourth round given their CBT status? That I'm not sold on. A multi-year contract at a lower annual salary is the much more likely path to Bednar returning to the Yankees.

Jazz Chisholm Jr., Yankees: Even in a down year, Chisholm was a 3.5-WAR player thanks to the breadth of his skill set. He hit 19 homers, he stole 41 bases, and he was fourth among second basemen with +13 outs above average. The all-around game and the fact that Chisholm will play the entire 2027 season at age 29 would seem to make him a slam dunk QO candidate. My sense is the Yankees won't commit any significant payroll to next season without first seeing what the new CBA brings, which is exactly what they did before the last lockout. I think the Yankees value the payroll flexibility (i.e. the certainty that Chisholm won't take the QO) more than the post-fourth round compensation pick they would receive if he signed elsewhere.

Adrian Morejon, Padres: Morejon will be an interesting test case for San Diego's new ownership. He is outstanding, one of the five or six best relievers in baseball, and he'll play the entire 2027 season at age 28. The QO would make Morejon the highest-paid reliever in the game, but only if he takes it, and his age and effectiveness would seem to make that unlikely. Do the Padres roll the dice and give Morejon the QO, and risk sinking $23.15 million into a (great) setup man, or not bother because they're only in line to receive a draft pick after the fourth round if he leaves? Díaz, Josh Hader (from the Padres), and Raisel Iglesias are the only relievers to get the QO in the last seven years. Is Morejon in that class?

#2706. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2705. Grading every NBA lottery pick's first two weeks as impressive 2026 rookie class dazzles early

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

If there's one takeaway from the first two weeks of the 2026-27 NBA season (other than the fact that there are way too many injuries), it might be this: this rookie class has the potential to be the best in league history. Maybe that's an overreaction and a case of recency bias, but the stats and film don't lie.

This group of players was heralded as one of the best freshmen classes in college basketball history. Not only did those players meet expectations, but they also went beyond them. It's hard to see a collection of talent hitting college basketball again like that for a long time.

Wizards forward AJ Dybantsa was late to the party, but the No. 1 overall pick finally made his debut last week against the Cavaliers after missing the first four games due to an ankle injury. Dybantsa scored 19 points in his first game while being on a minutes restriction.

The biggest surprise in the NBA is the Memphis Grizzlies, the only team in the association that hasn't suffered a loss. Cameron Boozer, who has seemingly won at every place he's played — whether in high school, Team USA, Duke and now the NBA — remains the favorite to win NBA Rookie of the Year over Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr. and Bulls forward Caleb Wilson.

With the first two weeks of the season in the books, it's time to assess the play of every lottery pick from the 2026 NBA Draft by handing out some early grades. Let's dive in, starting with Dybantsa.

It took exactly 16 seconds to showcase one of Dybantsa's elite skills: drawing contact at the rim. In 35 games last season at BYU, Dybantsa attempted 296 free throws, which ranked No. 1 among all college players. That's going to be a huge part of his game throughout his career because of how good he is at getting into the lane and drawing fouls. He has already attempted nine free throws in his first two games. Dybantsa is still on a minutes restriction.

AJ Dybantsa looking comfortable in his second career game 😯17 PTS | 8 REB 🔥 pic.twitter.com/px5FjLar5t

Once that restriction gets lifted, he will play even more than the 57 minutes he played during the first two games combined. The Wizards have a chance to be a sleeper play-in team in a loaded Eastern Conference this season.

Peterson's role with Utah is still being established. Something that stood out to me was Jazz coach Will Hardy benching Peterson for the final stretch against the Spurs last week, even though the game went to overtime and the team was already without Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen. There were a handful of plays in the fourth quarter where Peterson didn't make the right read on the defensive end, but the decision to bench the young rookie and only play him 26 minutes might've cost Utah a chance to steal a game at home.

Despite Peterson still trying to find a clear-cut role, he ranks fifth in his rookie class among field goals attempted (78) this season. Peterson thrives on-ball but is also very capable off the ball. That's why I really liked him as a fit with the Jazz. Peterson is going to figure it out.

Boozer is the ultimate winner. Since high school, Boozer has a 155-17 record across games in high school, at Duke and in the NBA. It should come as no surprise that he's contributing to winning at the highest level. Boozer had his first career triple-double (18/12/12) and followed it up with a career-high 27 points against Sacramento. Even when Boozer isn't playing well, he can still impact winning with his passing.

Cameron Boozer career-high 27 vs Kings:27 PTS | 9 REB | 1 BLK | 8/14 FG | 77 TS% pic.twitter.com/vRuH59q21R

He is an elite processor of the game and it's only going to get better throughout his career. The one concern I do have about Boozer is the rim finishing. Per Synergy, he is shooting 42.4% at the rim. Aside from that, Boozer has been awesome. If the Grizzlies keep winning, Boozer should be the favorite to win Rookie of the Year.

The Bulls are off to a slow start, but Wilson is not. The way he can impact both ends of the floor remains one of his strengths. Wilson is also fearless and won't back down from anybody. Two of my favorite plays so far from the NBA season came in Bulls vs. Celtics games. On the defensive end, Wilson recovered while Jayson Tatum was driving middle and rejected him at the rim with his off hand. In a game against Boston days before, Wilson had the ball at the top of the key against Paul George, jab-stepped left and dunked it while taking contact.

look at this block by Caleb Wilson on Tatum omg pic.twitter.com/1vSkEUhaOU

He is averaging 3.2 stocks (steals and blocks) per game. Another note: He is taking 7.8 (!) 3-pointers per game after taking 27 total attempts at North Carolina last season. The efficiency (29.8%) isn't there yet, but if Wilson's shooting ticks up, it changes his entire ceiling.

Wagler has been playing in a sixth man role during the first two weeks. The Clippers are trying to bring him along slowly. I'll say this: It's time to start Wagler. He has looked very comfortable even dating back to his first minutes against Sacramento. Wagler is shooting better from 3 (31.3%) than 2 (24%), but I'm not super worried about the efficiency for him or any rookie guard on the list for one reason: Rookie guards are historically inefficient.

Again, it's understandable why the Clippers want to wait to start Wagler, but it's time to put him in the starting lineup and play him even more. Wagler has shown he's capable of taking on that responsibility while running the second unit.

Similar to Wagler, Brown is coming off the bench to begin his career. He has played over 25 minutes just once this season due to the team placing him on a minutes restriction. Brown also didn't play against Indiana last weekend due to back injury management. In the game (against Boston), where Brown played over 25 minutes, he was electric in the fourth quarter. Brown scored 13 of his 17 points in the final frame, including a corner 3-pointer to send the game to overtime. Brown made a rookie mistake in overtime, attempting a layup with less than five seconds remaining, with his team up by one and the shot clock off.

After that miss, Tatum knocked down a game-winner. Brown had NBA range during his time at Louisville, and that was on display against the Celtics. It's just a matter of time before Brooklyn lifts the minutes restriction and throws him into the starting lineup.

Acuff has become the most polarizing rookie to talk about. The Kings are bad. Like, potentially the worst team in the league. However, Acuff has been the bright spot. His shotmaking is second-to-none in his class. When Acuff is hot, he can score at will. Acuff joined exclusive company earlier this week when he finished with 34 points and 14 assists against the Pelicans. The only other teenager in NBA history to post at least 30 points and 12 assists in a game, per CBS Sports research? LeBron James.

DARIUS. ACUFF. JR.Shakes his defender and drills the 3!A game-high 21 points through two quarters for the @SacramentoKings' rookie 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/hA98OwsWvL

Acuff has the ultimate green light in Sacramento. It's going to stay that way throughout his rookie season. It feels more like a matter of when, not if, Acuff scores 45+ points in a game. It might even come before the calendar flips to 2027

Flemings' best game came last week against Miami, when he finished with 23 points, five assists, five rebounds and a block/steal. Flemings' role with the Hawks this season was always going to be off the bench, so it shouldn't come as a surprise that he has scored 27 points combined in the other six games he has played in.

Flemings doesn't have to score to make an impact on the game. He was heralded as one of the best two-way players in the class, which was on display in his last game against New Orlenos when he recorded four steals. Flemings uses his speed to his advantage to get to the rim, create his own shot and change the pace. Despite taking six field goal attempts per game, Flemings has been very efficient (47.6%).

Johnson has come off the bench in his first six games under his former college coach, Dusty May. Although his numbers don't necessarily pop, Johnson is going to be a very impactful player, especially on the defensive end of the floor. He's capable of guarding 1-5, which is super valuable when/if the Mavs decide to switch everything on defense.

Burries is coming off the bench for the Bucks, which somewhat surprises me. He was awesome in summer league and should be playing more than 16 minutes per game.

THIS DUNK FROM BRAYDEN BURRIES🤯14 points for the @Bucks rookie off the bench tonight! pic.twitter.com/H3Jk99cKn3

Burries did have one of the highlights of the season so far with a poster dunk over Tristan Enaruna. That game was also the highest-scoring (14 points) game of his so far.

Lendeborg is one of the most entertaining players to watch. You either love him or hate him, but you're still going to watch. It should come as no surprise that it took him exactly one game to talk trash to the opponent, which nearly backfired when Luka Dončić went on to drop 37 points less than 10 days after the season opener.

The highs of Lendeborg's rookie season so far have been fantastic. Even though he had his worst statistical game against the Lakers, he finished with at least 25 points in three consecutive games, including a 31-point, 12-rebound outburst against the Nuggets. Yes, Lendeborg may be the oldest rookie from the first round of the draft, but it's clear to see why the Warriors drafted him. He is already Golden State's second-best player behind Steph Curry, which shouldn't even be that hot of a take. Lendeborg was awesome in a win over the Clippers and scored a career-high 37 points. He should be the co-favorite with Boozer for ROTY.

It's going to be sink-or-swim for Mara, with Chet Holmgren becoming the latest Thunder player to suffer an injury that will sideline him for multiple weeks. Mara logged 28 minutes against the Rockets and finished with seven points, nine rebounds and four blocks. Mara was one of the most efficient scorers at the rim and also one of the top shot blockers in college basketball because of his long 7-foot-3 frame. Mara has a chance to contribute in a larger role with Holmgren out. He's going to be just fine.

Ament was a DNP-CD in Ament's first two games before making his first appearance against the 76ers. Ament has skill and potential but is one of the rawest players drafted in the lottery. The Bucks are bringing him on slowly, which should do wonders for his development. He shot under 40% from the field last season at Tennessee but has been solid in that department (45.8% from the field, 44.4% from 3) in four games. The sample size isn't large enough to give a definitive grade, but Ament has shown signs of improvement since his college days. He has also been solid on the defensive end of the floor.

Steinbach has played in just two games this season, both of which came in garbage time. He played 12 minutes in a 121-81 loss to the Hawks and two minutes against the Wizards last week. Coming into the season, I expected Steinbach to play a larger role. That could still happen later in the season, but the sample size so far isn't large enough to hand out a letter grade.
